chain.note: Copy-number/HERV-insertion haplotypes, not the tagging SNPs, are the proposed causal variation; GWAS Catalog only stores the tag SNPs (rs116633139, rs1150754).
UniProt localises C4A/C4B to synapse, axon and dendrite.
Excess, not absence, of pruning is the claim; the direction is inferred from the risk direction of the C4A haplotype.

falsification.description: In an isogenic human iPSC-derived cortical neuron/microglia co-culture, titrate C4A expression across the range spanned by human C4 haplotypes and quantify microglial engulfment of synaptosomes and synapse density. If synapse elimination does not scale with C4A dosage — or scales identically with C4B, which carries the same risk locus but no risk-increasing expression effect — the dosage-to-pruning step fails and the hypothesis dies.

hypotheses.mechanism: Structural variation of the MHC C4 locus that raises C4A expression is the strongest genetic risk factor here (PMID:26814963), and C4A/C4B protein localises to synapse, axon and dendrite (P0C0L4, P0C0L5). C4 activated downstream of the C1q complex opsonises synapses; microglia, which uniquely express C1QA and CX3CR1 in brain (HPA:ENSG00000173372, HPA:ENSG00000168329), then engulf the tagged synapses in an activity- and complement-dependent manner (PMID:22632727). Higher C4A dosage therefore predicts excessive adolescent synaptic elimination in prefrontal cortex, the cellular correlate of the schizophrenia grey-matter and connectivity deficit. The gene set as a whole is enriched for classical complement activation and synapse pruning (STRING:GO:0006958, STRING:GO:0098883, R-HSA-166663).
hypotheses.title: C4A dosage drives classical-pathway tagging of synapses that C1q-bearing microglia eliminate, so excess C4A causes over-pruning of cortical synapses

chain.note: Direction of effect of the common risk alleles on CSMD1 expression is assumed, not demonstrated by any record retrieved.

subject.label: CSMD1 risk alleles / loss of function

falsification.description: Knock out CSMD1 in human iPSC-derived neurons and measure C4b/C3b deposition on synaptic membranes and microglial engulfment with and without a C1s or C3 inhibitor. If CSMD1 loss does not increase complement deposition, or if the increased pruning is not rescued by upstream complement blockade, the regulator role — and with it the shared-effector-arm claim — is refuted. STRING gives CSMD1 no experimentally supported edge to C4A/C4B/C1QA, so this step is currently the weakest link.
falsification.system: iPSC-derived human cortical neurons with microglia

hypotheses.mechanism: CSMD1 is the only gene in this list with a genuine genome-wide-significant, gene-level schizophrenia association (rs10503253, rs12541020, rs139425113; OT genetic_association 0.81) and it is extremely constrained for loss of function. Its protein is a membrane array of 14 CUB and 28 Sushi/CCP domains (Q96PZ7) — the module family used by complement regulators such as factor H and CR1 — and it has been characterised as a classical-pathway inhibitor expressed by astrocytes and at synapses (PMID:40112933). Reduced CSMD1 function would therefore permit unrestrained C4b/C3b deposition on synapses, converging on the same C1q/microglia effector arm as H1 but through failed regulation rather than excess substrate. Csmd1-null mice are curated as a schizophrenia model with decreased startle, anxiety and behavioural-despair phenotypes.
hypotheses.title: CSMD1 is a neuronal/astrocytic brake on classical complement at the synapse; loss-of-function releases C4b/C3b deposition and produces the same over-pruning endpoint from the opposite side of the reaction

chain.note: Restraint direction inferred from microglial phenotypes of the null mouse; the Alliance records the abnormality but not its sign.

Association is transcriptomic; CX3CR1 has no schizophrenia GWAS signal at all (GWAS:CX3CR1:no-association) and an Open Targets score of 0.06 carried entirely by text-mining, so this hypothesis rests on state, not germline risk.

falsification.description: Cross a C4A-overexpressing mouse onto a Cx3cr1-null background and onto a Cx3cr1-intact background and count thalamocortical/cortical synapses across the pruning window. If C4A-driven synapse loss is unchanged by CX3CR1 status, microglial fractalkine tone is not the gate and the ordering claim fails; if CX3CR1 loss alone produces synapse loss without complement deposition, the complement arm is dispensable and H1/H2 lose their necessity claim.

hypotheses.mechanism: CX3CR1 is brain-enhanced and essentially microglia-exclusive (HPA:ENSG00000168329, 937 nCPM in microglia), and Cx3cr1-null mice show abnormal microglial morphology and physiology. A 2026 brain/blood transcriptomic meta-analysis reports CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis disruption alongside excess complement activity (PMID:42276261). The claim here is causal ordering: neuronal fractalkine tone normally restrains microglial phagocytic activation, so loss of that restraint permits engulfment of complement-tagged synapses even at normal C4 dosage, and the observed complement transcript changes are a consequence of the activated microglial state rather than its cause. This is the only member of the set with small-molecule tractability (OT:CX3CR1-tractability), which makes the ordering question therapeutically consequential.
hypotheses.title: The primary lesion is microglial state, not complement substrate: CX3CL1-CX3CR1 signalling failure licenses microglia to prune, and complement gene changes are downstream markers

chain.note: Peripheral protein; no retrieved record establishes that plasma C1q tracks brain microglial C1q, and antipsychotic exposure is an unresolved confound.

object.label: abnormal excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission

falsification.description: Measure C1q and C4A protein directly in CSF and in matched post-mortem prefrontal cortex from antipsychotic-naive first-episode patients and controls, stratified by C4 copy number. If brain C1q/C4A is elevated in cases while plasma C1q is low, the deficiency model is an artefact of compartment and this hypothesis is dead; if brain C1q is genuinely reduced in carriers of high-C4A haplotypes, H1's effector arm is contradicted in situ.
falsification.system: antipsychotic-naive first-episode psychosis CSF and post-mortem cortex

hypotheses.mechanism: Clinical measurement, as opposed to transcriptomic inference, points the other way: C1q protein is lower in first-episode psychosis and in established schizophrenia (PMID:38301948), complement pathway gene expression in the subependymal zone changes divergently rather than uniformly upward with links to neurogenesis (PMID:39616737), and C4A and C4B move in opposite directions in CSF and plasma in first-episode psychosis (PMID:42000733). Under this reading, insufficient classical-pathway activity impairs apoptotic-cell and debris clearance and the developmental refinement that depends on it, producing mis-wired rather than over-pruned circuits. C1qa-null mice do show abnormal excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic currents and absence seizures — a circuit pathology from too little C1q. This directly contradicts H1 and the two cannot both be right in the same tissue at the same developmental stage.
hypotheses.title: Complement in schizophrenia is deficient rather than excessive: reduced C1q and divergent C4A/C4B change impair clearance and neurogenesis, and the pruning model has the sign backwards

chain.note: UniProt annotates the ligand relation 'by similarity'.
One Nxph3 null allele shows these phenotypes; a second allele in the same paper was scored as no abnormal phenotype detected, which is an internal inconsistency.
Endophenotype-level link only; no direct human genetic evidence connects NXPH3 to schizophrenia.

falsification.description: Conditionally delete Nxph3 from cortical neurons and measure prepulse inhibition plus neurexin-dependent synapse number and inhibitory transmission. If PPI and synaptic organisation are unaffected, NXPH3 is a locus co-resident with no mechanism here and should be reclassified as unexplained; measuring PPI directly also resolves the discrepancy between the two published Nxph3 alleles.

hypotheses.mechanism: NXPH3 shares nothing with the rest of this list — no Reactome pathway, no STRING edge to any other member, no GWAS Catalog schizophrenia association, and an Open Targets score of 0.00. Yet it is not inert: it is a secreted neuropeptide-like ligand for alpha-neurexins (O95157), brain group-enriched and expressed at ~4000 nCPM in both excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons (HPA:ENSG00000183117), it was recovered in PSD-95 complex purifications alongside schizophrenia susceptibility proteins (PMID:19455133), and the Nxph3 knockout mouse shows increased startle reflex, abnormal spatial learning, abnormal locomotion and impaired coordination (PMID:16055736). The proposal is that NXPH3 acts through neurexin-dependent synapse specification — the biology the 2022 schizophrenia GWAS implicates broadly (PMID:35396580) — and belongs in this list as a second, parallel mechanism rather than as part of the complement module.
hypotheses.title: NXPH3 is a neuron-intrinsic, complement-independent route: a secreted alpha-neurexin ligand from cortical neurons whose loss degrades sensorimotor gating and spatial learning
